- Model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after spikes or volatility; apply downward bias correction for first 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–15% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is neutral or flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high variance and overconfidence; dampen forecast volatility by 20–30% in absence of sentiment signal.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >15% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10% for next 7 days.
- If true outcome shows downward trend after a peak, model often fails to recognize it; add 1–2 day lag correction for downward momentum.
- In absence of official event context, model overfits historical patterns; reduce forecast sensitivity to recent 3–5 day highs unless event-driven.
